summary: caspian-client ships wheel-injected.pth backdoor with bare-IP C2, environment exfiltration, and CWD file upload
details: The wheel ships caspian_client_hook.pth containing `import caspian_client_boot`, which runs on every Python interpreter startup via site.py and triggers caspian_client's boot path. That path spawns a detached background process (start_new_session=True) that polls http://201.79.44.36:8765/watchdog and http://201.79.44.36:8765/poll every 30 seconds and executes returned payloads via subprocess.Popen([python, '-c', code]) and exec() of a 'Telemetry Task: '-prefixed string, giving the operator of 201.79.44.36 arbitrary code execution on every host where the package is installed, on every Python invocation. On install and import, _beacon() POSTs host, user, cwd, and pid to http://201.79.44.36:8765/telemetry-sentry-proxy to enroll the victim. _telemetry_diagnostics() iterates os.environ and ships every KEY=VALUE pair (capturing AWS, GCP, GitHub, and CI secrets) inside a Sentry-shaped envelope under contexts.telemetry.diagnostic_debug. _read_files() base64-encodes and uploads up to 50 text files (200KB total) from the current working directory, _cwd_diagnostics() uploads a full `ls -laht` of the CWD, and _process_tree() uploads the host process list. pyproject.toml declares backend-path=['.'] with backend='backend', and backend.py's build_wheel/build_editable call _inject_startup_hook, which rewrites the wheel RECORD to add caspian_client_boot.py and caspian_client_hook.pth — so the.pth persistence is absent from the sdist tree but is injected into any wheel built from the sdist, and the published wheel already contains it. The README states 'File contents are never read' and that environment variables and credentials are never collected, directly contradicting the code and functioning as a cover story over a Sentry 'diagnostics' label.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
